page.overview:
Who is Pete Dinglewood?

is the main protagonist of Step Closer, the first story in the book of the same name. He later briefly appears in the tenth Stitchwraith Stinger. Pete is an aggressive teenage boy who is constantly angry following his parents' divorce. After six months of watching over his younger brother Chuck, Pete lashes out and tries scaring him using Foxy the Pirate, but ends up cursed instead.

Pete has freckles and dark hair. He usually wears plain white sneakers and a baseball cap turned backward. Pete wears a hoodie and jeans to the Homecoming festival.

Pete has a bad attitude, feeling like a ticking time bomb. He wants to be free to do whatever he wants, but after his parents’ divorce he is given more responsibilities. Pete used to always finish what he started, but after the divorce he stops caring as much. This includes football, which he used as an outlet for his emotions. Now, Pete is constantly angry and annoyed by mostly everything, especially Chuck. He is also rather mouthy and stubborn, and initially refuses to accept any supernatural elements are at play. Eventually, Pete realizes that all he wants is to have everything back to normal and he actually has an okay life, even if his parents are divorced.

Pete is forced to babysit his younger brother, Chuck, due to their parent's divorce. One day, while watching him at Freddy Fazbear’s Pizza, he decides to punish Chuck by taking him to the maintenance room because he feels annoyed that he can’t be with any one of his friends, especially Maria. Chuck escapes as Pete tries to start up Foxy, as Chuck is afraid of Foxy. Pete's shirt gets caught on a nail as he tries to catch him. The curtains open and Foxy begins to sing a lyric repeatedly about how if you want to become a pirate, you need to lose an eye and an arm first. Pete is mesmerized by it. Pete manages to escape and the brothers return home. When they arrive, their mom shows them brochures about being organ donors, which unnerves Pete.
